events.whyItMatters: Curaleaf has stopped asking and formally commenced its hostile offer, mailing the bid circular and inviting Aurora holders to tender 0.3463 Curaleaf subordinate voting shares plus US$0.75 cash per share -- an implied US$4.00, about US$260m in total, a 45% premium to Aurora's 30-day VWAP and subject to a US$5.00 cap price -- with the offer open until 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time on December 1, 2026. That takes the outcome out of the boardroom and puts it in the hands of the shareholder register for three and a half months. Aurora's special committee has told holders to take no action for now and accused Curaleaf of pressuring shareholders, so the question is whether a defence or a rival bid arrives before the register decides for itself; the underlying argument has not changed -- Curaleaf is bidding for a cash pile plus an international medical footprint, a 110% premium once Aurora's balance-sheet cash is stripped out.

events.whyItMatters: BaFin has approved Uber's offer document, so the agreed combination becomes a running tender: EUR41.50 a share in cash, about EUR13bn of equity on 314m fully diluted shares, acceptance from 27 August to 5 November 2026 and a minimum threshold of only 50% plus one share including Uber's own holding. The premium depends entirely on where you start: roughly 108% over Delivery Hero's unaffected 8 May close and 127% over the unaffected three-month VWAP, but about 34% over the three-month VWAP into the launch, so most of the value is already in the price. The catch is duration -- settlement is guided only to the second half of 2027, with merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances across a combined 99-country, $236bn-GMV footprint still to come. Holders are being asked to accept a fixed cash price now and wait a year for it.

phases.headline: Uber Publishes Offer Document for its Takeover Offer for Delivery Hero
phases.priceReaction: EUR41.50 offer is c.108% above the unaffected 8 May 2026 close

phases.headline: Delivery Hero Board Recommends Holders Accept Uber Takeover Bid
Uber-Delivery Hero deal enters South Korean merger review

events.whyItMatters: Independence Realty Trust is issuing 3.8 of its own shares for each Centerspace share -- $60.46 a share, a 14.7% premium and about $2.14bn of equity -- to build an $8.1bn-enterprise-value, 163-community apartment REIT across 17 states. Because it is all stock, IRT holders are not being paid out; they are being diluted into a portfolio that is 58% Sunbelt, 27% Midwest and 15% Mountain West, which is a deliberate dilution of the pure Sunbelt exposure the market has been pricing IRT on. The case rests on G&A and scale synergies plus a Midwest book with less new supply than the Sunbelt; the risk is that investors who bought a Sunbelt operator now own something else. Closing is guided to as early as the end of Q4 2026.

phases.headline: Independence Realty Trust and Centerspace to Merge in $8.1 Billion Combination
Activist Irenic plans to vote against Independence Realty's purchase of Centerspace

events.whyItMatters: Grab is paying $1.49bn cash for 60% of Atome Financial, with the remaining 40% to follow roughly two years after the first close -- its largest push yet into lending and the point at which financial services stops being an add-on to mobility and deliveries. Atome brings buy-now-pay-later, consumer cash loans, cards and digital lending across Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand, and 25m cumulative transacted users to cross-sell into Grab's ecosystem. It also puts unsecured consumer credit risk on a platform whose investors have been valuing it on take-rate and GMV, in five markets where BNPL regulation is still moving. Closing is guided to Q3 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

phases.headline: Grab to acquire majority stake in Atome Financial, accelerating growth and profitability of Financial Services segment

events.whyItMatters: NextEra's $67bn all-stock purchase of Dominion is the largest regulated utility transaction ever announced, and the whole of it now turns on Virginia, where lawmakers and the public are arguing that AI data-center load growth will be paid for by households. The sweetener filed on 14 September doubles residential bill credits from two years to four, lifts the Virginia credit pool from $1.78bn to $1.87bn, adds $100m of shareholder money to Dominion's Energy Share hardship programme and promises 1,000 new jobs -- and pointedly funds the extension by redirecting credits that would otherwise have gone to data centers. Every concession is margin given away before closing, so the question for NEE holders is how much more the State Corporation Commission extracts, and whether the deal survives at a price that still earns its cost of capital.

phases.headline: NextEra, Dominion offer more Virginia bill credits and 1,000 new jobs to win approval for $67 billion merger
'A different deal on the table': AG Jay Jones asks SCC to reset the clock on Dominion-NextEra merger

events.counterparty: Sequence Holdings / DFO Management (Michael Dell family office)
events.whyItMatters: Michael Dell's family office and Sequence Holdings are paying $32.50 a share in cash -- about $4.6bn of equity on top of roughly $3.1bn of net debt, a $7.7bn enterprise value and an 88% premium to Baldwin's unaffected 17 June price -- to take one of the fastest-growing US insurance brokerages private. The timing is the point: the stock had already run 58% in three months and 35% year-to-date, so public holders are being cashed out at the top of that re-rating rather than riding the rest of it, and the 7.5% move on the day says the market reads $32.50 as close to the whole prize. Employee equity rolls into the private vehicle, which keeps the people who generate the commissions in the deal while the public register exits.

phases.headline: The Baldwin Group to Go Private Through Majority Investment by Sequence Holdings and Dell Family Office

events.whyItMatters: H.I.G. is taking the asset-inspection and testing group MISTRAS private at $20.35 a share, an $866m enterprise value including debt -- but at only an 8% premium to the 30-day VWAP and 13% to the 90-day. Almost the whole price is carried by the stock's own 61% run since the end of 2025 rather than by the buyer, which is what makes this a test of whether a board can sell a re-rated company cheaply to a sponsor. With voting and support agreements already locking up about 31% of the register, the 40-day go-shop expiring 27 October is the only realistic route to a higher number, and a deal that clears with an 8% premium sets the reference point for every other industrial mid-cap trading near its own highs.

phases.headline: MISTRAS Group, Inc. Enters into Definitive Agreement to Be Acquired by H.I.G. Capital for $20.35 Per Share in Cash
phases.priceReaction: +4.6% on the day on roughly 474x average volume

events.whyItMatters: Every regulatory condition in the ~$111bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement was already satisfied across 68 jurisdictions, and on 21 September the last obstacle -- the 12-state antitrust suit led by California AG Rob Bonta -- was settled, so the deal can finally close: Zaslav has told staff to expect completion no later than early October and Ellison has said roughly two weeks from the settlement. The price of getting there is a five-year court-enforceable behavioural package rather than divestitures: at least $1.5bn of additional domestic film spend, 30 theatrical releases a year for two years then 32 for three, a $30m payment for every film short of that floor, a $47.5m fund for workers displaced by the merger, no sale or closure of the Paramount or Warner Bros. lots in the Los Angeles area for five years, separate cable-carriage negotiations for each company's channels for five years, and an independent board over CBS News and CNN -- all policed by a five-state enforcement committee. Nothing structural was given up, so the combined asset base arrives intact, but the output floor and the spending commitments are now fixed charges against the synergy case, and Bonta was explicit that settling is not an endorsement. The ~$7m-a-day ticking fee to WBD holders runs until the deal actually closes.

events.whyItMatters: Spanish agri-food cooperative Dcoop has taken the lead in a multi-bidder auction for Madrid-listed Deoleo, offering about EUR470m (~$545m) for a 57% stake in the world's largest olive-oil bottler, owner of Bertolli and Carbonell, in a combination reported to carry more than EUR2.2bn of turnover. The competition file is the catch: to clear US antitrust Dcoop would have to sell the Bertolli and Carapelli brands, so the winner of the whole would have to break it up immediately. Nothing is agreed -- Italy's Coricelli, Bonifiche Ferraresi and Newlat Food, France's Lesieur (Avril) and Australia's Cobram Estate Olives are all still circling -- but the process is reported to be in its final stages, with a deal possible as early as September.

events.whyItMatters: Abu Dhabi's sovereign investor L'IMAD is offering Dh6.25 a share in cash -- a 23% premium to the Dh5.10 close, 25% above the one-month VWAP and 31% above the three-month VWAP, valuing AD Ports Group at roughly AED31.8bn ($8.66bn) -- to buy in the ~24.6% that its wholly owned ADQ does not already hold and take the group private. For minority holders it converts a stranded stake in a state-controlled operator into a full cash exit at a premium; for the market it removes the only listed vehicle through which outside investors can own Abu Dhabi's ports, logistics and maritime franchise. The board's appointment of HSBC as financial adviser is the first sign the offer will get a formal independent assessment rather than an automatic wave-through.

phases.headline: Announcement of Notification to Submit a Voluntary Conditional Cash Offer to Acquire AD Ports Group Shares at Dh6.25 per share, taking L'IMAD's holding through ADQ from 75.42% to up to 100%

events.whyItMatters: Aon is paying $17bn including debt -- $16.7bn net of roughly $278m of tax attributes -- for the tenth-largest US insurance broker, a business with about $3bn of annual revenue, more than 10,500 staff and close to 200 US offices, and funding all of it with new debt raised across a range of maturities rather than with equity. That is the investment question in one line: a broker still digesting the NFP purchase is levering up again to build what CEO Greg Case calls the premier US middle-market platform, against $395m of targeted annual run-rate net adjusted EBITDA from revenue and cost synergies. Middle-market commercial insurance is where organic growth and client retention hold up best, which is what the price is paying for; on the other side KKR and Caisse de depot exit a position taken private at $4.3bn in 2014 at about 3.4x their capital across the life of the investment. Closing is guided to the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approvals.

phases.headline: Aon to Acquire USI to Establish the Premier U.S. Middle Market Platform
phases.priceReaction: AON and KKR shares flat in the premarket

phases.headline: Aon Raises $13.5 Billion From Bond Sale to Fund USI Takeover

events.whyItMatters: Copart is paying $10.50 a share in cash -- about $1.9bn, a 45% premium -- through a tender offer for ACV Auctions, buying its way out of pure salvage and into the digital wholesale market for ordinary used dealer cars, with ACV run as an independent subsidiary and closing targeted by year-end.

phases.headline: Copart Nears $2 Billion Deal to Acquire ACV Auctions, Sources Say
Copart to Acquire ACV, Expanding Position Across the Vehicle Remarketing Ecosystem
Copart launches tender offer for ACV Auctions at $10.50 per share

events.whyItMatters: Telix is paying $1.65bn upfront -- about $1.25bn of it in new Telix shares, handing ITM holders 23.7% of the combined company -- plus up to $700m in milestones to own the only globally scaled commercial supplier of lutetium-177, turning its radiopharma pipeline's key input from a bought-in isotope into a captive, profitable production business.

phases.headline: Telix to Buy Isotope Maker ITM in Deal Worth Up to $2.35 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Artemis Gold, a single-asset producer only a year and a half into commercial production at Blackwater in British Columbia, is paying US$427m entirely in its own shares -- 0.0966 Artemis shares per Vista share, an implied US$2.83, a 29% premium to the 20-day VWAPs to 18 September -- for a company whose only real asset is still a feasibility-stage project. What it buys is Mt Todd in Australia's Northern Territory: 9.1m ounces of measured and indicated plus 1.4m inferred, already permitted for a 50,000 tonne-a-day plant, and a stated path to more than a million ounces of annual production. The trade for existing holders is dilution today against ounces that need a large capex decision and years of build before they earn anything, at a point in the gold cycle when paper is cheap to issue. Closing is targeted for January 2027 and needs 66-2/3% of Vista votes cast plus Australian FIRB clearance and Northern Territory ministerial consent.

phases.headline: Artemis Gold to Acquire Vista Gold in US$427 Million All-Stock Deal

events.whyItMatters: Generac has converted a generator franchise built on suburban home standby into an AI-infrastructure supply contract: $2.4bn of committed deliveries across 2027 and 2028 and up to $8bn over the life of a long-term backup-power agreement for Amazon's data centres, against group revenue of roughly $4bn a year. The structure is the point -- Generac granted Amazon warrants over up to 1,693,745 of its own shares at $200.93, about 308,000 exercisable at signing and the rest vesting as Amazon actually pays for generators, so the customer is compensated in Generac equity for the volume it delivers. The stock re-rated more than 40% on the news. It is the same warrant-linked template Oracle used with Bloom Energy in April, and it makes hyperscaler capex rather than the housing and storm cycle the swing factor in Generac's earnings -- with the concentration risk that comes with a single customer of that size.

phases.headline: Generac Shares Jump on $8 Billion Amazon Data Center Supply Pact
phases.priceReaction: GNRC +40% in extended trading, up about 19% the following session

events.counterparty: Thomas Priore investor group (Searchlight Capital Partners)
events.whyItMatters: Priority's own chairman and CEO is buying the payments-and-banking-technology company he runs, at $8.05 a share in cash for the stock his group does not already own -- about $1.6bn of enterprise value, a 38% premium to the 18 September close and 65% above the price before his first approach was disclosed in November 2025. The special committee's leverage shows in the gap between that and where he started: the final price is more than 30% above his opening $6.00-$6.15 range, and Searchlight Capital Partners' equity commitment removes any financing condition. Minority holders get a clean exit but give up the fintech's recurring embedded-banking revenue at a mid-cap multiple; completion needs a majority of unaffiliated shareholders and regulatory clearance, with delisting from Nasdaq guided to the first half of 2027 -- a long window in which a competing bid, or a vote against, is the only remaining source of upside.

phases.headline: Priority Technology to go private in $1.6 billion CEO-led deal

events.whyItMatters: Cognex is paying roughly $500m in cash, entirely from existing cash and investments, for the depth-sensing camera business Intel founded in 2014 and spun out in 2025 -- its move out of factory-floor machine vision and into robotic perception and 'physical AI'. RealSense should do $80-90m of revenue in 2026, more than 50% growth, into a robotic-perception market Cognex sizes at about $600m today and $1.6bn by 2030. The price is roughly 6x forward sales plus a $56.5m three-year cash retention pool and about $50m of restricted stock for RealSense staff, and the market read the combination as expensive rather than strategic: the shares fell about 5% on the day. The investment case now rests on whether depth perception and robot navigation attach to Cognex's installed industrial base faster than they commoditise.

phases.headline: Cognex to Acquire RealSense, Expanding Machine Vision Leadership into High-Growth Robotic Perception Market

events.whyItMatters: Kone's EUR29.4bn cash-and-share purchase of Germany's TK Elevator, agreed in April, would create the world's largest lift maker and roughly double a company currently worth about EUR30bn -- which is precisely why it is now being fought jurisdiction by jurisdiction rather than in the boardroom. The UK Competition and Markets Authority has begun inviting third-party views ahead of a phase 1 case, while the US Department of Justice has already opened an in-depth review that can run a year or more; completion is targeted for the second quarter of 2027. For Kone holders the deal is the whole equity story for the next 18 months: the synergy case is large enough to re-rate the shares, and the remedy risk -- service-portfolio divestitures in overlapping European and North American markets -- is large enough to hollow it out before it arrives.

phases.headline: Kone-TK Elevator deal faces UK antitrust review

events.whyItMatters: Merck KGaA is buying a US life-science tools and reagents franchise outright for $73 a share in cash, an $11.3bn enterprise value at a 36% premium to Bio-Techne's one-month VWAP, and with the US antitrust waiting period expired and ~78% of shares voted in favour the remaining risk is foreign regulatory clearance rather than price or shareholder consent.

phases.headline: Germany's Merck to buy Bio-Techne for $73 per share
Bio-Techne Shareholders Approve Acquisition by Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany

events.whyItMatters: Iridium holders have voted to fold the L-band satellite network into Rocket Lab for $27 in cash plus collared Rocket Lab stock (a notional $54 a share), so the remaining questions are regulatory timing to a mid-2027 close and how much of the consideration's value rides on Rocket Lab's own share price.

phases.headline: Iridium Stockholders Approve Acquisition by Rocket Lab

events.whyItMatters: A BASF takeover of Evonik would be the biggest consolidation in German chemicals in years, and RAG-Stiftung's roughly 43.8% stake -- not Evonik's board, which says there are no talks -- decides whether it happens.

events.whyItMatters: Harworth's board has stopped resisting and Peel's 187p best-and-final cash offer (a 30% premium to the undisturbed price) will give it majority control within days, capping the upside for remaining holders.

phases.headline: Harworth backs Peel's £632m best and final takeover offer
Peel Pepper offer for Harworth Group declared unconditional

events.whyItMatters: Akamai's largest contract ever -- $11.6bn over seven years with a $9bn option -- recasts it as an AI-infrastructure name, paid for with about $1.7bn of extra 2026 capex and a warrant for roughly 5% of the company.

phases.headline: Akamai lands $11.6 billion Anthropic deal, shares soar

events.whyItMatters: A day after Barry Diller's People Inc. dropped its own $48.30-a-share bid for MGM, the Wall Street Journal reports MGM is weighing a reverse takeover of People -- a way for MGM to buy back the roughly 27% of itself that People owns (worth about $2.5bn against People's ~$2.7bn market value) and pick up the media and Turo stakes almost for free, which is why People's holders, not MGM's, have the most to gain if an offer materialises.

phases.headline: MGM Resorts Is Discussing Making a Bid for People: WSJ

events.whyItMatters: People Inc. has withdrawn its June proposal to buy the ~73% of MGM Resorts it does not own at $48.30 a share in cash (more than $18bn), citing the debt the deal would have required, which removes the take-private floor under MGM's shares while leaving Diller's 27% stake and his stated openness to 'a strategic transaction' hanging over the register.

phases.headline: MGM Resorts shares sink 11% after Barry Diller's People Inc. rescinds takeover offer

events.whyItMatters: Lear has lifted its repurchase authorisation from about $600m remaining to $1.5bn and extended it to the end of 2029 -- roughly 26% of its market capitalisation -- signalling that management sees its own shares as the best use of free cash flow for an auto-seating and e-systems supplier that has already retired about 60% of its share count since 2011.

phases.headline: Lear Increases Share Repurchase Authorization to $1.5 Billion and Extends Authorization

events.whyItMatters: Gold Fields has put a price on Australia's largest gold miner -- 0.3125 Gold Fields shares plus A$7.25 cash per share, about A$38.7bn and a 22% premium to the 11 September close -- and Northern Star's board has unanimously rejected it as opportunistic, mostly paper and heavily conditional. The stock still trading below the implied value after a 10% jump says the market doubts a knockout bid, but with Elliott already pushing for a strategy and board review, Northern Star is now in play: the question is whether Gold Fields sweetens the cash component or a rival emerges.

phases.headline: Australia's Northern Star rejects $27 billion takeover approach from Gold Fields
phases.priceReaction: +10.6% to A$24.46 in early Monday trading, below the implied offer value

phases.headline: Gold Fields Said to Weigh Sweetening Northern Star Bid With Cash

events.whyItMatters: A $150bn top-up -- the largest buyback authorization increase ever -- lifts Nvidia's remaining capacity to $235bn through fiscal 2028, turning AI-driven cash generation into a structural per-share tailwind and signalling management sees more cash than it can deploy into capex and investments.

phases.headline: Nvidia Boosts Share Buyback Authorization by $150 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Selling 30% of NIO Power to rival Geely for its Yiyi Power swap business plus RMB640m cash sets a ~RMB16bn ($2.4bn) valuation on Nio's costliest infrastructure bet and brings a second major automaker's cars onto its battery-swap network, shifting the network from a Nio-only cash drain toward a shared industry utility.

phases.headline: Geely To Buy 30% Stake in Rival Nio's Battery-Swapping Unit

events.whyItMatters: TotalEnergies is lifting Q4 buybacks to $2.5bn (from $1.5bn in Q3) and committing to grow the dividend more than 5% a year through 2030, locking a larger share of $100 oil windfall cash into shareholder returns rather than capex.

phases.headline: TotalEnergies raises buybacks and pledges higher dividends as oil trades around $100

events.whyItMatters: AMD is paying $8.2bn in its own stock -- its second-largest deal after Xilinx -- for Fei-Fei Li's spatial-intelligence model lab, buying model-research talent and a foothold in physical AI and robotics so its chip roadmap is shaped by where frontier models are heading rather than by Nvidia's lead; holders take the dilution, and the payoff depends on retaining a research team that is the whole asset.

phases.headline: AMD to Buy Fei-Fei Li's World Labs Startup for $8.2 Billion

events.whyItMatters: AstraZeneca is putting $2bn into Summit at $18.36 a share (about 12% of the common) and pairing its ADCs with ivonescimab, which removes Summit's funding overhang without giving up ivonescimab economics and puts a big-pharma validation -- and a natural future acquirer -- on the PD-1/VEGF bet.

phases.headline: AstraZeneca Makes $2 Billion Strategic Equity Investment in Summit Therapeutics

events.whyItMatters: Berlin is selling about 75% of nationalised gas importer Uniper, and a joint non-binding KKR-RWE bid -- a reversal of RWE's August stance, against Equinor and a Brookfield-CPP consortium -- makes a trade sale over an IPO more likely and would hand Germany's largest utility a big gas and power-plant fleet.

phases.headline: KKR, RWE Submit Joint Bid for Germany's State-Owned Uniper, Sources Say

events.whyItMatters: RHI Magnesita's 470p cash plus 0.028 shares proposal (about 549p, a 47% premium, ~£1.37bn) would combine the two biggest listed refractory makers, and with Cevian's 23% stake irrevocably committed if the board recommends, the deal now hinges on the Vesuvius board and a 27 October put-up-or-shut-up deadline.

phases.headline: RHI Magnesita confirms talks for 549p offer for Vesuvius

events.whyItMatters: The largest rare-earths producer outside China is paying about A$968m in its own shares -- 0.0207 Lynas shares per Meteoric share, a 68% premium -- for Caldeira in Brazil, one of the world's largest ionic-clay deposits, lifting Lynas' measured-and-indicated resources by 79% and reserves by about 26%; it buys a second jurisdiction and heavy-rare-earth feed outside Malaysia and Australia, but Lynas holders take dilution today for a project that still needs years of capex, which is why Lynas fell about 5% while Meteoric jumped 50%. Meteoric votes in January 2027 with implementation targeted for March.

phases.headline: Lynas in $968m deal to acquire Meteoric Resources

events.whyItMatters: Transurban is spending A$4.5bn of debt-funded cash to buy out CPP Investments' 25% of NorthWestern Roads Group (M7, NorthConnex) and 10.5% of WestConnex, taking it to 75% and 60.5% control of Sydney's core motorway network; more of its cash flow now comes from assets it already runs, with no equity raise and FY27 distributions guided unaffected, but leverage rises and the ACCC must clear a deal that deepens an existing Sydney toll-road near-monopoly before completion in 2027.

phases.headline: Transurban to buy $4.5 billion of Sydney toll-road stakes from CPP Investments

events.whyItMatters: Hormel is paying about $1.055bn in cash and new debt for a family-owned value-added chicken processor with ~$1.2bn of sales, lifting chicken from under 5% to about 13% of its protein mix; it is a bet on the fastest-growing protein, but accretion is not expected until fiscal 2028 and both S&P (to BBB+) and Moody's (to A3) downgraded Hormel because leverage temporarily moves above its 1.5-2.0x target.

phases.headline: Hormel Foods agrees to acquire Brakebush for $1.06 billion

events.whyItMatters: The US DOJ closed its second-request investigation into Transocean's $5.8bn all-stock purchase of Valaris (15.235 RIG shares per VAL share) without remedies, clearing the biggest hurdle to creating an offshore driller worth about $17bn in enterprise value that will own a large share of the high-spec floater and jackup fleet; with only Brazil left, a Q4 2026 close now looks likely, and the combined fleet gives the new company far more pricing power in deepwater contracting.

phases.headline: Transocean, Valaris receive US antitrust approval

events.whyItMatters: Having just finished a C$7bn repurchase on 25 September, TD intends to buy back up to another C$10bn (up to 61m shares, about 3.7% of the count) by July 2027, subject to OSFI approval -- a sign the bank is still sitting on surplus capital from its Schwab stake sale and US balance-sheet restrictions, and is returning it rather than redeploying it while its US growth is capped.

phases.headline: TD Bank to buy back up to $10 billion of its shares
